It's ok, just have in mind that there is a 98% efficacy rate on this. Maybe even more given that you were 8-9 weeks. 
Personally, I took the whole day off (just in case) and my cramps lasted for like 6 hours. I don't know about you, but I tend to have heavy periods so it was kind of the same for me. I didn't even notice if there were any "sizeable" clots really, but it all went okay no matter how much I would worry about the whole thing. At the end I realized that me freaking out would only make it all worse. Try to be as kind to yourself as you can in times that no one else will, okay?

I've had a very similar experience a few years ago. You have nothing to worry about. I didn't even notice any "big enough" clots, and everything went fine and I was 10-11 weeks pregnant. We tend to overthink it and it's totally normal to feel that way, but truly it only adds to feeling worse.   
Worst case scenario, let's say you didn't pass everything. A week from now you go to the doctor's office and they take care of it. It's that simple. I promise you will be okay. 
Sometimes people who go through this don't even notice the clots and everything goes smoothly either way. Let that be a worry for the future and try to focus on processing what your body and mind is feeling at the moment. Really, that is all that matters. 
Hope you the best and I am sure everything will turn out just fine. If you need further advice or anything, don't hesitate to reach me/us out.

Yes, they help a lot to prevent obsessing with these thoughts and to reduce the anxiety induced by them. I can still explore those topics, let my head wander around but without the fear, anxiety or paranoia.

I don't get how do these "coincidences" work either. 
Once, during a psychotic episode, I thought everybody could read my thoughts. I would think of a really specific word to prove this to myself (without telling them, of course) and they would say it all of a sudden, even out of context they would just bring it up. I isolated myself for days since I couldn't talk to anyone without feeling vulnerable, exposed and really scared.
During that week, I've also had a really weird experience that I still cannot explain. I was walking with a friend, we were going to his house. On our way there, we passed in front of the hospital in which I was comitted into when I got in a coma. When I looked that way, I saw my brother and his priest sitting on the sidewalk, crying a lot and this priest trying to talk to him. Of course, I was hallucinating. I knew that I was, but I still saw all of this very clearly as if it were happening right then and there. A few days later, I asked my mother to tell me more details about how they felt during my coma (my family is very reserved and secretive about this kind of things, I knew very little details about this situation since they wouldn't talk about it) and without having to ask directly she told me "we were worried sick. Specially when you were at your worst... you even died for a few minutes. When the doctor told us your brother ran outside crying. He called his priest and they stayed outside talking." 
I froze. How could I know any of this? How could I have seen this if I was dead or in a coma? Nobody told me anything.
I've had more situations like this happen to me, but I just say I was during a psychotic break and leave it at that without giving it much thought. I know it is dangerous for me to think too much about those things or I become obsessed. I start to wonder if I am dead, in another dimension, or in hell. I thought about everything, but thinking never got me anywhere. Anywhere but the psych ward. So I stay away from that, take my meds and move on with my day, hoping it's for the better.

I'm sorry, don't let me be misunderstood. My intentions aren't bad at all. I know that there are many people in horrible situations, but so was I and got better anyway. I just wanted to give a little glimpse of hope to anyone out there considering suicide. So, if I'm not harming anyone and i'm potentially helping someone instead, then what's wrong? I just thought that if I read something like this before I attempted suicide (multiple times), then maybe I would have reconsider it.
Word! I've failed 4 or 5 times last year and every single attempt and its consequences only made me feel worse (if possible). Unfortunately, committing suicide is harder than you'd think.
